channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Como sobrevivem os partidos que não recebem Fundo Partidário: doações, filiados e outras receitas bancam gastos
item.description: Nine Brazilian parties survive almost without the Party Fund, relying on donations, member contributions and other revenues to finance their activities. DC was the highest earner among them, with R$ 2.8 million in 2025, nearly all from individual donations, while Mobiliza and PRTB spent more than they raised. PSTU relied primarily on member contributions, which accounted for 75% of its revenue.

item.title: Presidente do TSE reúne institutos de pesquisa para tratar de critérios de levantamentos eleitorais nesta terça-feira
item.description: TSE President Kassio Nunes Marques is meeting with electoral research institutes on Tuesday to discuss criteria for conducting and publishing voter intention polls, aiming to prevent data contamination and judicial disputes. The meeting follows the May suspension of an AtlasIntel poll and seeks to establish guidelines on technology, verbal neutrality, and digital research flow, with most institutes represented by a lawyer from ABEP.

item.title: Janja descarta que cargo formal seja solução para sua atuação
item.description: First Lady Janja stated she does not see holding a formal government position as necessary for her role, emphasizing that her work is already regulated for transparency. She explained she maintains a regular work routine at the Palácio do Planalto, attending meetings, trips, and inter-ministerial articulations, with her agenda publicly disclosed daily. Janja also noted that media coverage often focuses on her personal life and international travels rather than her institutional activities.

item.title: Se direita vencer eleição, haverá interrupção democrática, diz ministro
item.description: The Minister of Entrepreneurship, Paulo Henrique Pereira, warned that a right-wing victory in the 2026 presidential elections could trigger a 'wave of democratic interruption' affecting an entire generation. He emphasized the importance of the alliance with the PT to counter what he described as an still-active and dangerous far-right, noting that Brazil narrowly escaped a coup and cannot afford to repeat the risk.

item.title: 'Bolsonaro é quem vai colocar a faixa de presidente em mim', diz Flávio sobre a possibilidade de vencer as eleições
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, PL pre-candidate for president, stated in a live broadcast that if he wins the October 2026 election, his father, Jair Bolsonaro, will place the presidential sash on him during the January 2027 inauguration, despite the former president serving house arrest for attempting a coup. Flávio expressed confidence that his father’s legal situation will be reversed and pledged to 'rescue Brazil,' criticizing Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes for restricting his visits to his father after a letter of support was shared on social media.

item.title: Janja presta solidariedade a Damares e Michelle Bolsonaro após ataques: ‘Não importa o campo ideológico’
item.description: First Lady Janja da Silva expressed solidarity with Senator Damares Alves and former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro following misogynistic attacks, stating that political violence against women has no ideological boundary. She emphasized that misogyny affects all women equally, regardless of political alignment, during an interview on UOL’s Frente a Frente program.

item.title: Rede pede a Fachin que suspenda mudança de prazo da Lei da Ficha Limpa
item.description: The Rede Sustentabilidade party has requested that STF President Minister Luiz Edson Fachin grant an injunction to suspend the effects of Complementary Law 219 of 2025, which changes the calculation of the Ficha Limpa ineligibility period to start from the date of conviction rather than the completion of the sentence. The party argues urgency due to the approaching 2026 party conventions and the recess of rapporteur Minister Cármen Lúcia, who has already voted to declare the law unconstitutional, calling it a blatant setback for administrative morality.

item.title: Janja diz que apelido de “gastadeira” é “misoginia pura”
item.description: First Lady Rosângela Lula da Silva, known as Janja, stated that the nickname 'gastadeira' used against her is a pure example of misogyny, explaining that she travels in executive class for security reasons mandated by the Federal Police, not personal choice. She emphasized her active role in the Presidency, attending meetings, undertaking official trips, and maintaining a public agenda, noting that this model of engagement still causes surprise in Brazilian society. Janja also urged the approval of a bill to criminalize misogyny, currently stalled in the Chamber of Deputees, and noted that the TCU unanimously archived four processes regarding her international travel expenses since 2023, finding no evidence of misuse of public funds.

item.title: Flávio pede que OAB se manifeste após Moraes suspender visitas a Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) called on the Brazilian Bar Association (OAB) to take a stance after Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended, for 90 days, the right to visit former President Jair Bolsonaro, following Flávio’s public reading of a letter from his father, which violated a court order banning third-party social media use. Flávio, who formally joined Bolsonaro’s legal defense team in March, argues the suspension infringes on his constitutional right as a lawyer to communicate with his client, even if he is the senator’s son. The measure was imposed because Bolsonaro is under house arrest and prohibited from using social media, including through intermediaries.

item.title: Zema cobra fim de politicagem em post da CBF
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) criticized the Brazilian Football Confederation's (CBF) post honoring the national team after its World Cup elimination, accusing it of politicization. Zema argued the post strayed from sports into political territory, which he deemed inappropriate. He urged sports institutions to remain neutral and focus solely on athletic matters.

item.title: Lula acusa EUA de "pirataria" por anunciar que cobrará taxa em Ormuz
item.description: President Lula accused the United States of becoming a 'pirate' nation if it imposes fees on ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, as announced by Donald Trump. The statement was made on Monday (13) and reflects growing tensions in trade and maritime navigation between the two countries.

item.title: Renan Santos chama Moraes de 'marqueteiro' e 'cabo eleitoral' de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Renan Santos, a pre-candidate for president from the Missão party, criticized the decision by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to prohibit Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting former president Jair Bolsonaro, calling the justice a 'political marketer' and 'campaign operative' for Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Lula diz que não vai ter tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: President Lula stated that there will be no US tariff hike on Brazilian products, despite expectations of new tariffs up to 25% on Brazilian exports, linked to a USTR investigation into alleged illegal trade practices, including Pix. The comment was made after his visit to the first ethanol-powered turbine project (UGEE1000BR) in São José dos Campos, developed by IAE/DCTA, attended by officials including Alckmin, Silveira, Boulos, Mercadante, and Marina Silva.

item.title: Por que Lula pôde divulgar cartas quando estava preso? ex-advogado de petista responde
item.description: Lula's former lawyer, Manoel Caetano Ferreira, states that Lula's disclosure of letters while imprisoned in 2018-2019 was lawful because no judicial restriction barred his communication, unlike Bolsonaro's current situation, which involves violating precautionary measures. The comparison between the two cases is legally unfounded, as Lula was not subject to any communication ban. Lula's 2018 letter endorsed Fernando Haddad, while Bolsonaro's 2026 letter supported Flávio Bolsonaro, prompting Moraes to prohibit visits.

item.title: Lula critica atuação dos EUA no Estreito de Ormuz e classifica cobranças como ‘pirataria’
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva strongly criticized recent U.S. proposals to impose fees on maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, labeling them as acts of 'piracy'. He emphasized that the Strait of Hormuz is a critical artery for global energy trade, through which about one-fifth of the world's consumed oil passes, and warned that such measures undermine free navigation and international stability.

item.title: A resposta pública de Flávio à decisão de Moraes sobre visita a Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro accused Justice Alexandre de Moraes of attempting to interfere in the 2026 elections by banning, for 90 days, visits from his father, Jair Bolsonaro, under house arrest, following the public disclosure of a letter by the former president. Flávio called the move an effort to isolate his father and suggested the timing was deliberate to harm his electoral prospects. Moraes defended the decision, stating that sharing the letter on social media violated house arrest rules and could constitute premature electoral propaganda.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro diz que lei Magnitsky contra Moraes deve ser restabelecida
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro urged the reinstatement of the U.S. Magnitsky Act against Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, arguing that the suspension of visits from Flávio Bolsonaro to his father, Jair Bolsonaro, constitutes political abuse and undermines the democratic legitimacy of the 2026 elections. The sanctions, previously applied in 2023 and lifted in December, targeted Moraes and his wife over alleged human rights abuses. Eduardo, residing in the U.S. and facing charges in Brazil for attempting to obstruct his father’s trial, is lobbying the Trump administration to reimpose the measures.

item.title: Renan Santos chama Moraes de ‘marqueteiro’ e ‘cabo eleitoral’ de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Renan Santos, a pré-candidate for President from the Mission party, criticized Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to ban Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting Jair Bolsonaro, arguing it strengthens bolsonarism by fostering a persecution narrative. He compared it to Lula's support for Haddad in 2018 and claimed Moraes acts as Flávio Bolsonaro's 'electoral cabo' and 'marketer', diverting attention from scandals like the Banco Master case.

item.title: Lula diz não acreditar que haverá novo tarifaço dos EUA contra o Brasil
item.description: President Lula stated he does not believe the United States will impose a new 25% tariff on Brazilian products, despite the USTR’s recommendation to apply the surcharge due to trade imbalances linked to digital trade, Pix, intellectual property, and deforestation. The final decision rests with President Donald Trump and is expected by July 15. Lula made the remark at an event in São José dos Campos, two days before the USTR’s final recommendation.

item.title: “Você, enquanto juíza, dando opiniões num regime. O que queria? Flores?”
item.description: Former federal deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL) criticized former judge Ludmila Lins Grilo after she questioned the pre-campaign strategy of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) to disseminate a letter from former President Jair Bolsonaro (PL), who is under house arrest. Eduardo accused the judge of acting with partisanship in an authoritarian regime, using irony by asking if she 'wanted flowers' instead of allowing the former president's communication. The incident highlights tensions between Bolsonaro's circle and the judiciary.

item.title: Janja: o Brasil nunca teve uma primeira-dama que trabalhasse efetivamente
item.description: First Lady Rosângela da Silva, known as Janja, defended her active role in the Lula government, stating that Brazil has never had a first lady who worked effectively. She attributed criticism to society and the press not being accustomed to the presidential spouse’s active participation, citing class prejudice as a underlying factor. Janja emphasized her daily work schedule, official agendas, international trips, and initiatives against hunger and menstrual poverty, while dismissing cost-related accusations as misogynistic.

item.title: Janja diz que críticas sobre gastos no exterior são 'misoginia' e afirma ser a única primeira-dama do Brasil que 'trabalha efetivamente'
item.description: First Lady Janja Lula da Silva defended her international travels and government work, labeling criticisms of being a 'spendthrift' as misogyny and class prejudice. She stated she is Brazil's first first lady to work 'effectively,' with an office at the Planalto Palace and a daily public agenda, and compared her trajectory to that of Ruth Cardoso, emphasizing her humble origins and public university education.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro: "Magnitsky contra Moraes deve ser restabelecida"
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro criticized Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to suspend visits from Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro, proposing the application of the Magnitsky Act against Moraes. He argued that banning communication between a jailed presidential candidate and his son constitutes political interference and undermines the democratic legitimacy of the 2026 elections. The STF's measure followed the dissemination of a letter from Jair Bolsonaro supporting Flávio's candidacy, which violated a judicial order prohibiting the ex-president from using social media directly or through intermediaries.

item.title: Pesquisa BTG/Nexus: Desejo por terceira via dispara para 27%
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows that preference for a third-way candidate in the 2026 Brazilian elections rose from 11% in March to 27% in July, reflecting growing dissatisfaction with options tied to Lula and Bolsonaro. Although the first round is not yet defined, this significant increase suggests a potential reconfiguration of Brazil's electoral landscape.

item.title: Zema cita 'farra suja' em post da CBF após eliminação do Brasil na Copa: 'Comecem acabando com essa politicagem'
item.description: Romeu Zema, a presidential pre-candidate and former governor of Minas Gerais, criticized the CBF in comments on an institutional video, accusing the organization of prioritizing accountability to Brasília over Brazilian fans and of being subjected to 'politicagem' and 'dirty dealing'. He reiterated claims that Francisco Mendes, son of Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes, exerts undue influence over the CBF, citing an alleged agreement between the IDP (linked to Mendes' family) and the CBF, and influence on Neymar's call-up. Zema linked these allegations to a 2024 decision by Gilmar Mendes that restored the CBF's leadership.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro: Moraes quer só 'desculpinha' para tirar meu pai da domiciliar
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, accused Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes of seeking only a 'little excuse' to remove his father, Jair Bolsonaro, from house arrest. He claimed there is alleged interference by the minister in the 2026 elections, suggesting the judicial decision is politically motivated to harm the Bolsonaro family's candidacy.

item.title: Flávio pede que OAB se manifeste após ser impedido de visitar Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) said he will request the OAB to act after Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended his 90-day visits to imprisoned former President Jair Bolsonaro. He claims the decision hinders his professional activity as his father's lawyer and violates the inviolable right of lawyer-client communication, despite their familial relationship. The suspension followed Flávio's publication of a letter from Jair Bolsonaro endorsing his 2026 presidential candidacy, which Moraes views as circumventing the ban on the ex-president's public statements through third parties.

item.title: Flávio diz que ato de Moraes é ‘desculpinha’ para tirar pai da domiciliar e interferir nas eleições
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) accused Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes of interfering in the 2026 elections by suspending his 90-day visitation rights to his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a sentence for attempted coup in home confinement. Flávio claimed Moraes is seeking a mere 'excuse' to revoke the house arrest and blame him, drawing a parallel to Lula’s ability to run in the 2022 elections while imprisoned.

item.title: “Moraes quer interferir na eleição“, diz Flávio sobre restrição a Jair
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro accused Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes of attempting to interfere in the 2026 elections by imposing a 90-day ban on visits to his father, Jair Bolsonaro, after the latter’s letter endorsing Flávio’s presidential candidacy was shared online. He called the measure disproportionate and baseless, arguing it unfairly isolates Jair Bolsonaro and questioning why similar prior disclosures did not trigger STF action.

item.title: TSE promove Semana Nacional do Sistema Eletrônico de Votação
item.description: The TSE is promoting the National Week of the Electronic Voting System from August 3 to 9, with activities across the 27 Regional Electoral Tribunals to increase public awareness of the transparency, security, and auditability of Brazil's electoral process. The week will conclude with the Democracy Run in Brasília on August 9.

item.title: Flávio acusa Moraes de tentar “interferir nas eleições”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro accused Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes of attempting to interfere in the 2026 elections by banning him from visiting former President Jair Bolsonaro for 90 days, calling the measure disproportionate in a YouTube live stream.

item.title: Lula afirma que Santos Dumont teve a história roubada pelos EUA
item.description: President Lula claimed that the US stole Santos Dumont's historical credit as the inventor of the airplane, arguing that Dumont was the first to fly the 14-Bis in 1906 without external assistance, unlike the Wright brothers. He said he will seek to restore international recognition of the Brazilian inventor in talks with French President Emmanuel Macron in October and framed the flight as a symbol of national pride and technological advancement.

item.title: Flávio diz que carta de Bolsonaro foi o quinto recado público do pai e acusa Moraes de interferir na eleição
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro accused Minister Alexandre de Moraes of interfering in the elections by banning visits to his father, Jair Bolsonaro, following the release of a fifth public letter from the former president endorsing his presidential bid. He argued that the four prior letters were published without objection from the minister and questioned why only this fifth letter triggered judicial action, insisting there is no difference between sharing it on his social media or through other media outlets.

item.title: Flávio diz que Moraes quer apenas 'uma desculpinha' para retirar Bolsonaro da prisão domiciliar: 'não vamos ser ingênuos'
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro accused Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes of seeking only 'a little excuse' to keep former President Jair Bolsonaro under house arrest and block communication with his son, claiming the 90-day suspension of visits aims to prevent Flávio from speaking with his father until after the first round of the 2026 elections. He called the decision disproportionate and a clear attempt to interfere in the electoral process, leaving the former president incommunicado.

item.title: Operação da PF sobre emendas é política e não há prova de desvios, diz Eduardo Cunha
item.description: Former Chamber of Deputies president Eduardo Cunha (Republicanos-MG) accused the Federal Police of conducting a politically motivated investigation into alleged illicit interference in the direction of parliamentary amendments. He denied any involvement in alleged misappropriation of funds and stated there is no evidence to support the accusations. The statement was given to Folha de S.Paulo on Monday (13).

item.title: Flávio irrita PL do Rio por agenda com família aliada de Paes enquanto direita aguarda definição sobre Senado
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro angered Rio's PL by meeting with the Reis family, allies of Eduardo Paes, in Duque de Caxias without informing state leadership or pre-candidate Douglas Ruas. The meeting occurred as the party awaits his decision on the Senate candidacy, with Carlos Portinho and Carlos Jordy as leading options, while the right-wing ticket faces uncertainty in the other Senate seat due to the case involving Márcio Canella.

item.title: Noruega é recepcionada por 90 mil torcedores em última "remada viking"
item.description: The Norwegian national team was welcomed by approximately 90,000 fans in Oslo after being eliminated by England in the 2026 World Cup quarterfinals. The event featured the final 'Viking row' celebration, a team tradition, as Norway achieved its best-ever World Cup run, including a historic 2-1 victory over Brazil in the round of 16.

item.title: Governo brasileiro envia toneladas de alimentos para Cuba, que vive profunda crise econômica
item.description: The Brazilian government has sent 48 tons of powdered milk to Cuba via the Brazilian Air Force, responding to the island’s worsening economic and humanitarian crisis exacerbated by U.S. sanctions under Donald Trump. The first flight departed from Canoas, Rio Grande do Sul, on Monday with 14 tons, and a second flight carrying 32 tons will leave from Porto Alegre on Tuesday, both bound for Santiago de Cuba. Coordinated by the Brazilian Cooperation Agency (ABC) and the National Supply Company (Conab), the effort involves senior Lula administration officials and continues Brazil’s pattern of humanitarian aid to Cuba and other Latin American nations.

item.title: Flávio: Moraes tenta “interferir nas eleições” ao proibir visitas a Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) accused Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes of interfering in the 2026 elections by suspending his 90-day prison visits to his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest. Flávio claimed the timing — preventing contact until after the first round — is no coincidence and alleges Moraes is using the visit ban as a pretext to keep Bolsonaro imprisoned. He argued the decision came after he published a letter from his father endorsing his presidential bid, which Moraes viewed as an indirect public statement violating Bolsonaro’s silence order.

item.title: Flávio critica decisão que impede se reunir com Bolsonaro e diz que Moraes quer ‘interferir nas eleições’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) criticized Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes' decision to ban him from meeting with former President Jair Bolsonaro for 90 days, calling it disproportionate and an attempt to interfere in the 2026 elections. He stated he could only resume communication with his father after the first round and questioned the rationale behind the 90-day period, suggesting it is not coincidental. The ruling followed Flávio's public reading of a letter from Jair Bolsonaro written during house arrest, which Moraes deemed premature electoral propaganda.

item.title: Veja o que Eduardo Cunha disse sobre cidades de Minas em mensagens
item.description: The Federal Police found messages from former Chamber of Deputies president Eduardo Cunha in which he directed the allocation of parliamentary amendments to municipalities in Minas Gerais, including Manhuaçu, Governador Valadares and Lajinha, in exchanges with server Mariângela Fialek. The messages were used by Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino to suspend payments and block over R$6 million from Cunha, who is running for federal deputy from Minas Gerais in 2026. Cunha also complained about alleged misattribution of amendments to Nikolas Ferreira and redirected funds to other towns such as Matias Barbosa, Pedrinópolis and Varjão de Minas.

item.title: Ao vivo: Flávio comenta decisão de Moraes de proibir visita a Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) will hold a live stream on Monday, July 13, 2026, to comment on a decision by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes that banned in-person visits to his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, after Flávio shared on social media a letter written by Bolsonaro during a visit. The 90-day restriction, lasting until October 11, prevents Flávio from seeing his father in person until after the first round of the 2026 elections on October 4. Moraes ruled that Flávio used the visit to circumvent the ban on Jair Bolsonaro’s use of social media, either directly or through intermediaries.

item.title: Governo confirma reunião do CNPE para 3ª feira após adiamentos
item.description: After four consecutive postponements, the National Energy Policy Council (CNPE) will meet on Tuesday, July 14, 2026, to approve raising the mandatory ethanol blend in gasoline from 30% to 32% (E32), alongside discussions on fraud prevention in the fuel market, voluntary biodiesel use, biodiesel import limits, and financing for Angra 3 nuclear plant. The meeting, chaired by Minister Alexandre Silveira, had its agenda adjusted after Petrobras-led removal of a Union gas auction item.

item.title: Carta a Flávio viola restrição e pode levar Bolsonaro de volta para cadeia, dizem especialistas
item.description: Experts say a letter in which Jair Bolsonaro reaffirmed Flávio Bolsonaro as his spokesperson and candidate may violate judicial restrictions and jeopardize his house arrest. Published in July 2026, the letter was seen as an attempt to influence the electoral process despite legal limitations imposed on the former president. Folha de S.Paulo noted that any political articulation could be considered a breach of precautionary measures.

item.title: Governo Lula envia nova remessa de ajuda humanitária a Cuba
item.description: The Lula government sent 48 tons of powdered milk to Cuba in two shipments via the Brazilian Air Force, coordinated by the ABC and supported by Conab, marking Brazil’s third humanitarian aid mission to the island in 2026 amid its supply crisis. The operation was agreed upon in a July 9 ministerial meeting and focuses on non-perishable food, explicitly ruling out energy aid due to U.S. sanctions risks on Petrobras if it supplied fuel to Cuba.

item.title: Bolsonaro copia carta de Lula, mas não apaga crimes que o tiraram das redes
item.description: From detention in Brasília, Jair Bolsonaro released a 'Letter to Brazilians' mimicking the title and format of Lula's 2018 'Letter to the Brazilian People', naming his eldest son as his presidential candidate for 2026. The move comes while he remains ineligible due to convictions for abuse of power and misuse of media, which bar him from running in elections.

item.title: Decisão de Moraes vai aumentar intenções de voto de Flávio Bolsonaro, diz presidente do PL
item.description: PL party president Valdemar Costa Neto claims that Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to ban Flávio Bolsonaro from visiting his father for 90 days after the senator shared a letter from the ex-president endorsing his candidacy will increase Flávio's voter intentions for the 2026 presidential race. He argues the move, seen as an attempt to politically silence the Bolsonaro family, will trigger a backlash reflected in upcoming polls. Flávio Bolsonaro's lawyers denounced the decision as unconstitutional, violating penal execution law, the Statute of the Bar, and the Constitution by denying familial visitation rights.

item.title: Moraes autoriza Braga Netto a fazer curso à distância para reduzir pena
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes authorized former Defense Minister Braga Netto to take remote courses and participate in a prison reading program to reduce his sentence. Braga Netto, who ran as Bolsonaro’s vice-presidential candidate in 2022, was sentenced to 26 years for his role in the 2022 election coup plot. The ruling, supported by the PGR, allows him to study project management, risk and strategic planning, and earn up to 48 days of sentence reduction per year through approved reading and validation by the prison’s validation committee.

item.title: As possíveis implicações contra Flávio após carta de Bolsonaro
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes has ordered the Electoral Attorney General's Office to rule on a video by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in which he read a letter from former President Jair Bolsonaro declaring him his 'spokesperson', considered potential premature electoral propaganda. While there is no risk of ineligibility or criminal punishment, the PGE may impose a fine between R$5,000 and R$25,000 if it finds the content exceeds legal limits. The video was released amid a family crisis after Michelle Bolsonaro accused Flávio of humiliating her, damaging his standing among female voters.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil deixará de ser “exportador de matéria-prima”
item.description: President Lula stated that Brazil will no longer export raw materials and advocated for the domestic industrialization of critical minerals and rare earths, emphasizing the need to add value to natural resources. He stressed that exploration of these minerals must occur within the country, citing historical examples of gold, silver, and iron, and highlighted the importance of the Armed Forces in protecting national sovereignty, including borders, oil, and underground wealth.
